correctness.rationale: The conditional reduced ODE is specified, not an unproven claim about arbitrary microscopic networks. At a positive equilibrium, t=K prod x_i gives x_i=t/(t+d_i) and K=Phi_d(t)=prod(t+d_i)/t^{D-1}. The unique minimizer solves sum d_i/(t+d_i)=1, since its derivative changes from 1-D to 1 monotonically. The Jacobian is similar by diagonal x_i sqrt(d_i) to -diag(t+d_i)+sqrt(d) sqrt(d)^T; rank-one inertia proves upper branch attracting and lower branch one-unstable, with one zero eigenvalue at threshold. At t_c, envelope differentiation gives partial log K_c / partial d_i = q_i=1/(t_c+d_i), strictly antitone in d_i, proving Schur concavity. For X, implicit differentiation gives partial log X_c / partial d_i=q_i^2/R-q_i with R=sum d_k/(t+d_k)^2. The derivative difference equals (q_i-q_j)((q_i+q_j)/R-1); tR=sum x_k(1-x_k)<1 and t(q_i+q_j)=x_i+x_j>1 for D>=3 because sum x=D-1 and other D-2 entries <1. Thus this factor is positive and gives strict Schur concavity. At equal widths t=(D-1)m, K_c=m D^D/(D-1)^(D-1), X_c=((D-1)/D)^D; a sequence approaching (S,0,...,0) gives K_c down to S and X_c to zero. Tangent Hessian and sum x=D-1 yield the same relative -sum eps_i²/(2D²) in both observables. Independent numerical roots for d=(1,1,1), (.5,1,1.5), (.1,.1,2.8) give K=6.75,6.554959921,4.55625 and X=.296296,.287297,.175583; symmetric perturbation errors decrease approximately quartically. Analytic derivative inequalities, not these numerical instances, prove strict global majorization.
